interpretation: Nectar gelsemine reduces robber exploitation and can reduce legitimate pollinator use/preference, but reward compensation and natural-versus-supra-natural concentration alter the magnitude or detectability of pollinator cost.
notes: Robber entry and within-plant exploitation are distinct decision stages. Do not collapse high-gelsemine and reward-compensated assays into one D state.

interpretation: Aconitum nectar alkaloids produce large B. terrestris consumption deterrence by the 20-ppm checkpoint, whereas the source places the sharp B. hortorum visitation decline around roughly 200–380 ppm.
notes: Raw lab dose cells support the low antagonist threshold. Deposited field visitation remains negatively associated with alkaloids but the exact source-model subset is unresolved; qualitative threshold ordering is source-verified.

interpretation: Floral 2-phenylethanol deters damaging ants; moderate expression increases nectar standing crop without detected pollination cost, whereas high expression reduces bumblebee visitation and pollination.
notes: Ordered expression levels support a guarded window before pollinator interference rather than one universal D-to-pollinator sign.

interpretation: All four marginal routes are estimable in one individual-plant panel, but their confidence intervals cross zero and the D-to-antagonism point estimate is opposite to the expected defence direction. The direct A×D reproductive-component estimates also have opposite point signs with both CIs crossing zero.
notes: Keep as the unique strict direct-A×D cluster but do not force a guarded/interference or shared-tracking label from unresolved slopes.

interpretation: More dilute nectar is associated with reduced bumblebee nectar robbing while legitimate hummingbird pollinators show no detected deterrence in the same focal system.
notes: This is an explicit same-system counterexample to universal pollinator interference; no claim is made that rho exceeds iota because route effects are on different endpoints.

interpretation: Nectar cardenolides reduce monarch oviposition but not monarch flower foraging; bumblebees show no avoidance in a single bout at the highest natural concentration, whereas colony-level deterrence emerges after several days.
notes: Both exposure duration and antagonist response construct alter the observed D state, so a single ordered dose-window label is less defensible than context_switching.

interpretation: Nectar-repellent chemistry reduces nectar-thieving ant visitation. For legitimate pollinators, the same chemical context reduces residence time and nectar removal yet can increase visit number.
notes: Visit number and use intensity have opposite signs within one experiment; generic pollinator-response pooling would destroy the mechanism.

interpretation: Benzylacetone scent increases M. sexta pollinator-mediated seed production and also increases M. sexta oviposition, establishing shared tracking for that consumer. Hyles lineata pollination shows little scent dependence, so the A-side regime changes with pollinator identity.
notes: The fully crossed scent×nectar phenotype is not strict direct A×D because nectar removal is a reward restriction rather than an independently justified defence axis.

interpretation: Experimentally enhanced floral fragrance increases florivore attraction but does not produce a detected increase in pollinator attraction in the same experiment; seed production declines under the enhanced-fragrance treatment context.
notes: Because both consumer routes were tested, the absence of a detected pollinator increase is informative rather than missing evidence.

interpretation: Within Cucurbita, floral sesquiterpenoids positively predict specialist squash-bee visitation and specialist flower-beetle use in the same comparative panel.
notes: The two source-reported coefficients have different numerical scales and are not subtracted; the regime classification uses only their source-verified positive directions.
